King Cake

Served at: Twelfth Night · New Year's Day · Epiphany (Three Kings Day)

Serves 8-10Prep 30 minCook 25 min

King Cake is a festive pastry traditionally served during the Epiphany season, including Twelfth Night, New Year's Day, and Three Kings Day. This colorful, sweet cake symbolizes the arrival of the Three Wise Men and is a beloved tradition in many cultures, especially in Louisiana and parts of Europe.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup warm whole milk (240 ml)
  • 2 1/4 teaspoons active dry yeast (1 packet)
  • 1/2 cup granulated sugar (100 g), divided
  • 1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened (113 g), divided
  • 5 cups all-purpose flour (600 g), divided
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 5 large eggs, room temperature
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1 teaspoon grated orange zest
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 cup cream cheese, softened (115 g)
  • 1/4 cup powdered sugar (30 g)
  • 1/4 cup brown sugar (50 g)
  • 1 tablespoon ground cinnamon
  • 1 large plastic baby figurine or dried bean (optional)
  • For icing:
  • 1 cup powdered sugar (120 g)
  • 2-3 tablespoons milk
  • Food coloring in purple, green, and gold
  • Colored sugar or sprinkles in purple, green, and gold

Method

  1. In a small bowl, combine warm milk, yeast, and 1 tablespoon sugar. Let sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  2. In a large bowl, mix 4 cups flour, remaining sugar, and salt.
  3. Add yeast mixture, 1/4 cup softened butter, eggs, vanilla, orange zest, and cinnamon to the flour mixture. Stir until combined.
  4. Knead dough on a floured surface, adding remaining flour as needed, until smooth and elastic, about 8-10 minutes.
  5. Place dough in a greased bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place until doubled in size, about 1 to 1.5 hours.
  6. While dough rises, prepare filling by mixing cream cheese, powdered sugar, brown sugar, and cinnamon until smooth.
  7. Punch down dough and roll into a large rectangle about 12x18 inches (30x45 cm). Spread filling evenly over dough.
  8. Roll dough tightly from long edge into a log. Form into a ring and pinch ends together to seal. Place on a greased baking sheet.
  9. If desired, hide the baby figurine or bean inside the dough at this point.
  10. Cover and let rise again for 30-45 minutes until puffy.
  11. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Brush dough with remaining softened butter.
  12. Bake for 25-30 minutes until golden brown. Cool completely on a wire rack.
  13. Mix powdered sugar and milk to make a thick glaze. Divide glaze into three bowls and color each with purple, green, and gold food coloring.
  14. Drizzle glaze over cooled cake and immediately sprinkle colored sugars in traditional Mardi Gras colors.
  15. Serve at room temperature.

Tips

  • Use a plastic baby figurine for safety and easy removal after serving.
  • For a quicker version, use store-bought brioche dough or cinnamon roll dough.
  • The person who finds the baby in their slice traditionally hosts the next King Cake party or provides the next cake.
